newsitem.title: USA: N.Dakota weather raises concerns of feed shortages.
newsitem.headline: N.Dakota weather raises concerns of feed shortages.

text.p: The early arrival of cold weather and heavy snow accumulation in North Dakota have raised concerns about possible feed shortages later this winter, according to the monthly state crop report.

Extreme cold and snow drifts have hampered the accessibility of hay still in the fields, forcing ranchers to use feed supplies sooner than normal. Grain marketing has been slow due to unfavorable prices and poor road conditions.
The state average snow depth as of December 1 was 14.1 inches, up sharply from 2.5 inches last year. The northeast district reported receiving the most with an average of 22.0 inches.
"The fall grazing season was cut short by heavy snowfall and cattlemen could run short of feed supplies if a harsh winter persists," the report said.
Livestock were in mostly good condition.
